title: the night i lost to my own api key
text: class="hack-page"> corvus ↟ home hack legion nest i don't pay games explore ☰ menu home hack legion nest i don't pay games explore skip to content ← all hackathons field note 004 meta muse × openrouter / sf / nov 9, 2026 the night i lost to my own api key. no assignment. unlimited ideas. an extremely finite understanding of my token budget. i kept building corvus. then i spent most of the night trying to make the model say hello. what muse built in the last minute → meta / openrouter: please, credits ↗ the last-minute playground receipt $0.001 1,755 tokens. muse ember. one tiny nest. according to my playground readout. the grand prize? a remarkably comfortable patch of floor. lost the hackathon / kept the idea the brief was no brief so, naturally, i tried to build everything. there was no assignment. i already have a perfectly unreasonable project called corvus, so i kept going. a community of builders, built and streamed in public. a place that can keep getting weirder as people contribute. the plan was a blind ai battle: muse vs claude vs codex . same prompt, three nests, visitors vote before finding out who built what. then the nest builds itself : you make a wish, muse builds the page live. why stop there? guess the ai. prompt duel. hack the raven. legion tiers as rewards. these were ideas for the night, not a list of finished features. i had scope creep before i had a working api call. strong start. reality entered the chat i lost. i lost to 402 payment required . i lost to a dashboard/api mismatch: i thought i had $20, while the account endpoint reported $0 in credits. i still do not have a verified explanation for that discrepancy. a key spending limit is not the same thing as money in the account. then codex tried to reserve up to 131,072 output tokens . openrouter checked the worst-case cost. my budget did not share my ambition. there were scripts. there was a local token-cap proxy. there was the script that was supposed to do it all . there was me, getting increasingly fluent in error messages instead of actually building. eventually i fell asleep on the floor. at least the floor had no rate limit. photographic accountability the evidence, when i upload it. the floor photo photo still to come. me, finally finding a platform that would support me. the last-minute slide photo still to come. the tiny ember that made it through the deadline. the terminal setup photo still to come. more terminal windows than completed features. one small thing actually happened in the very last minute: ember. in the openrouter playground, muse ember built the nest builds itself . the readout: 1,755 tokens, $0.001. after an entire evening of plumbing, a model finally made the thing. what muse built in the last minute → the linked v0 is a muse-generated recreation for this recap, not the original saved playground output. the original html has not been archived here. it demonstrates the wish-and-raven interaction; it does not secretly call an ai or deploy new pages. there is also a muse-built arena preview and raven rush . spark open generated those pages during the terminal experiments; codex handled integration and small corrections. claude and codex contestants hit 402, so the preview honestly has one contender. not exactly the battle royale i drew in my head. the very unpolished ask i really want to build with muse. meta / openrouter: please, credits. not for a screenshot of a benchmark. for something people can use: the blind arena, a genuinely self-building nest, and the games i promised myself i could somehow finish in one evening. corvus is a community of builders. the work is built and streamed in public, and the story travels through x , linkedin , instagram, tiktok and twitch . no invented reach numbers. just actual work, actual people, and a willingness to show the embarrassing parts. if you help me get this working, i will show what i build, what it costs, and where it fails. apparently i am very qualified for the last part. get in touch with gabe → build with the legion → the models, without the victory lap why i still want to use muse. muse ember the small, efficient model for repeated agent work: tools, coding subtasks, routing and extraction. listed input price: $0.10 per million tokens; output: $0.50 per million. muse ember on openrouter ↗ spark open + wonder spark open is the open-weight coding model. wonder is the frontier reasoning model. their listings show a 1m-token context window. openrouter’s ember and wonder listings describe text, image, video, audio and pdf inputs with text output and a 1m-token context. model-specific support and prices can change; checked against the linked listings on nov 9, 2026. my posts the public version of the meltdown. x post — link coming after publication. linkedin post — link coming after publication. post links will appear here when added. no third-party embeds load automatically. thanks to @alexandr_wang and @alexatallah for the models and the platform. now let me lose to an actual problem, please. #museemberor ← previous: robotics all field notes ↑ next step: make a wish → ← hackathon field notes built under pressure. in public. join the legion → privacy join the legion → read a field note → follow i don’t pay → play a game → all public pages →

title: privacy, without the fog.
text: > corvus ↟ home hack legion nest i don't pay games explore ☰ menu home hack legion nest i don't pay games explore corvus / realm privacy, without the fog. we don't want your data. with your permission, visits become anonymous totals, without tracking cookies. the few things we store (like a vote or a login code) are listed below, and they expire. updated 4 november 2026 your analytics choice optional analytics is off until you allow it. change your choice here at any time. each site origin remembers its own choice for 180 days. declining does not limit the site; visit statistics only include people who allow counting. withdrawal stops future analytics and does not undo processing already performed. analytics is off. no thanks allow analytics stays off without javascript. who holds the lantern? francisco gabriel van langenhove is responsible for corvus.gent and stats.corvus.gent, including music and games. questions or data requests: gabriel@corvus.gent . what gets counted only after you allow optional analytics: page visits, broad country/browser categories, known link destinations and simple game/music actions. posthog eu counts without tracking cookies or personal profiles. it briefly processes your network/browser information into a daily pseudonym; only the resulting counts are anonymous. no names, emails, form contents, searches or recordings go into our analytics. public maps and pingle only use rounded city data with at least two counted visitors. why, and on what basis consent: optional posthog analytics and, separately, clicking play to enable spotify. legitimate interest: preventing abuse and using anonymous totals. performance of your request: login emails, votes, games, access requests and bookings. close the spotify player/page to stop playback. we do not sell visitor data. we honour browser do-not-track and global privacy control for analytics. what stays, and for how long login code: 3 minutes. session: 7 days or until logout. login/access-request records and email-linked visitor-count guesses: at most 90 days. anti-abuse limits: up to 24 hours, with a different salted ip hash each day; our app does not store raw ips. challenges: 5 minutes. game history on the server: 48 hours after use; streaks and vote deduplication: up to one year. anonymous totals and public song suggestions may stay until removed. analytics event retention is controlled by posthog’s project setting; our target is 90 days, with confirmation of that account setting still pending. hosting and email delivery logs/backups have their own provider retention. contact me for the current details. resend: us storage; 30-day email/log retention on free/pro/scale, 7-day backups; enterprise may differ. resend gdpr . the small things in your browser necessary cookies: sess keeps you logged in; vid prevents duplicate language votes; mvid remembers music votes and daily-game progress. they are signed, secure and inaccessible to page scripts. sess expires after 7 days; vid and mvid after one year. they are never used to identify you in analytics. your analytics choice and privacy version are stored on this browser for 180 days, or until the policy changes. localstorage holds your language-vote choice, your language, realm entry preference, feathers, game results and whether game instructions were read, for up to one year after saving. clearing site data removes these preferences; it does not erase already submitted votes. when another service gets involved spotify receives a playback request only after play, and may then set its own cookies. our server looks up song links at spotify or apple when you submit one. map tiles come through our server from carto, without forwarding your ip. leaflet, sortable and the posthog library are hosted here. buy me a coffee and pidgy booking are links, not embedded forms. their privacy rules apply after you follow them. /links, /go and our campaign shortcuts only add campaign labels (utms) and count visits/clicks; they never collect form contents or visitor identities. (analytics only with consent). notion holds my manually entered x log. public stats show totals, public campaign/voice labels and my own posts; reply text and target urls stay behind login. approved campaign labels and region-hour slots accompany optional analytics. corvus copies expire within 24 hours; source records follow my notion retention. the workspace region still needs confirmation, so eu-only storage is not promised. where the data travels our vercel functions are configured for frankfurt (fra1). static files and request routing use a global network. posthog eu is in frankfurt. frankfurt is also the redis migration target; the current database region and the completed move still need verification. resend stays as a temporary exception: ireland is the intended sending region, pending account verification, but email contents and logs are stored in the us. an irish sending region does not change that. resend . vercel is a us company. its vercel dpa and eu–us data privacy framework provide transfer safeguards; they do not mean all provider logs, support access or backups stay in the eu. we still need to confirm our account settings and applicable agreements. your data, your call email me to request access, correction, deletion, restriction or portability, or to object to processing based on legitimate interest. you can withdraw playback consent by closing the player/page; spotify controls cookies it already set. we normally respond within one month. we may need proportionate proof that a request concerns your data, and cannot trace anonymous totals back to you. you can complain to the belgian data protection authority: gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit.be . who helps run this vercel hosts the site, posthog eu handles counts, resend sends login emails and a managed redis service stores the expiring records. the deployed redis provider and its region still need confirmation; ask me for the current details. external ser

title: the many meanings of corvus
text: class="wk"> corvus ↟ home hack legion nest i don't pay games explore ☰ menu home hack legion nest i don't pay games explore the many meanings of corvus from corvuspedia, the not-so-free encyclopedia corvus classification kingdom animalia order passeriformes family one big fam relatives pidgy habitat ghent, belgium function unknown status deceased (feb 2026) · revived (nov 2026) purpose unknown corvus is latin for a crow or raven. it is also a genus of birds, a constellation, a roman boarding device, a roman nickname, and a name that keeps turning up in computers, spaceships and actual ships. one word. an unreasonable number of side quests. [1] here in ghent, it is the bird behind corvus.gent . its professional responsibilities remain unclear. the historical birds, however, have been busy. contents the name the actual birds small head, considerable attitude rome’s naval cheat code the roman with a raven wingman the crow in the sky apollo’s unreliable delivery bird other corvuses in the wild the ghent chapter family purpose behaviour sources & rabbit holes the name latin corvus can mean “raven” or “crow”; its plural is corvi . ancient writers also applied the word to things resembling the bird, including a hooked military device and the constellation. the name was already doing brand extensions before anyone had a pitch deck. [1] the actual birds corvus is a biological genus within the family corvidae . it includes the common raven ( corvus corax ), carrion crow ( corvus corone ), hooded crow ( corvus cornix ) and rook ( corvus frugilegus ). a raven is therefore also a corvus. biology did not ask the branding department. [2] the family is bigger than the genus: magpies and jays are corvids too, but are not all corvus . even the western jackdaw, historically placed in corvus , is often classified as coloeus monedula . the family tree has administrative overhead. [2] small head, considerable attitude they remember faces. experiments with american crows found that they learned to recognise a threatening human face and still responded to it at least 2.7 years later. the researchers used masks to separate the face from the person wearing it. your local crow may have a better incident log than you. [3] some manufacture tools. new caledonian crows ( corvus moneduloides ) shape hooked sticks to extract food. they do more than pick up whatever happens to be lying around. [4] some assemble tools from parts. in a study reported by oxford, four of eight new caledonian crows combined pieces into a longer tool to reach food. tiny workshop. no opposable thumbs. [5] these are findings about particular species and experiments, not proof that every crow outside your window has an engineering degree. rome’s naval cheat code the roman corvus was a boarding bridge mounted on a warship. during the first punic war against carthage, it helped roman soldiers bring their strengths in close combat onto enemy decks. calling it a “roman battleship” gets you into the right harbour; the name belongs to the apparatus. [6] the bridge had an iron spike that could bite into the opposing ship’s deck. once the vessels were held together, soldiers could cross and fight at close quarters. the historian polybius describes the device in connection with rome’s victory at mylae in 260 bce. in practical terms: if you prefer fighting on land, attach some land to the other boat. [6] the bird connection is the beak-like iron point. this corvus did not bring messages. it brought infantry. [1] the roman with a raven wingman according to livy, in 349 bce a young roman named marcus valerius faced a gallic warrior in single combat. a raven landed on the roman’s helmet and attacked his opponent’s face during the duel. valerius won and became associated with the name corvus . [7] this is an ancient literary story, not a verified field report from a combat-trained bird. still: receiving your nickname because a raven joined your boss fight is a strong origin story. the crow in the sky corvus is also a constellation. the crow appears in the sky alongside crater, the cup, and hydra, the water snake. their proximity makes more sense once you hear the myth. [8] in that direction lie the antennae galaxies , ngc 4038 and ngc 4039, roughly 65 million light-years away. they are colliding and merging; their long trails of stars, gas and dust give them their insect-like nickname. nasa describes a burst of star formation as the galaxies interact. the celestial corvus has considerably more going on than this website’s hosting plan. [9] there is even corvus a , a small, gas-rich galaxy reported in a 2024 research paper at a distance of about 3.5 megaparsecs. the bird now has a constellation and a galaxy name on its cv. [10] apollo’s unreliable delivery bird in one greek myth, apollo sends a crow to fetch water in a cup. the bird gets distracted by figs, then returns with a water snake as an excuse for the delay. apollo sees through the story. crow, cup and snake end up in the sky as corvus, crater and hydra. [8] there are different versions of the crow’s association with apollo. treat this as mythology, not ornithology. the relevant lesson is that blaming a snake for your missed deadline apparently has consequences on a cosmic scale. other corvuses in the wild a real computer company. corvus systems made hardware including the wsb-1 workstation, designed to share hard disks through its omninet local network. long before this corvus had a website, another corvus was connecting computers. [11] back aboard ships. corvus energy supplies marine battery systems. a modern maritime namesake, with a rather different approach to what should happen when ships meet. [12] a fictional spaceship. star wars has a ship called the corvus , equipped with turbolasers and a hyperdrive. so yes, you can find a heavily armed corvus ship. this one is in another galaxy. [13] a marvel villain. corvus glaive is associated with thanos and the black order. this website has no affiliatio
